knowledge.statement: In the same executed five-node StopSign run, node 4 - which never accepted the StopSign before the sync - ended at decided 5, accepted 5 and is_reconfigured true after re-decision, while node 5, which had already accepted and decided the StopSign, ended at decided 5, accepted 6 and is_reconfigured false. The control comparison (node 4 reconfig true) holds; the comparison requiring accepted 5 on node 5 is violated.
knowledge.conditions: Five OmniPaxos instances; entries 1..4 decided; reconfigure to configuration_id 2; AcceptStopSign and Decide withheld from node 4, delivered to node 5; node 2 elected at decided 4; node 5 reconnects via reconnected(2); held Accepted replies then re-decide index 5.

interpretations.rationale: The control run confirms both the failure and its boundary. Receipt 603faa15c86645c6a56b0b9fadfc0751 ran decided_stopsign_flips_through_reconnect_sync (exit 0, test passed). Event 0 (ready) establishes the premise: node 5 at decided 5, accepted 5, is_reconfigured true, node 2 at decided 4 with accepted 5. Event 1 (after_sync) shows node 5 at decided 4, accepted 6, is_reconfigured false; event 2 (after_redecide) shows node 5 at decided 5, accepted 6, is_reconfigured false, and the declared comparison requiring accepted 5 there is complete and violated. Event 3 (control) shows node 4 - which never accepted the StopSign - at decided 5, accepted 5, is_reconfigured true, and the control comparison holds. The boundary is therefore exactly the source prediction: the +1 that sync_log applies for log_sync.stopsign is correct when the follower's sync_idx precedes the StopSign (node 4, 4+1=5) but double counts when the follower's accepted prefix already includes it (node 5, sync_idx 5 plus one). On node 5 the StopSign remains accepted at 5 while accepted_idx becomes 6, decided can reach at most 5 because nothing may follow the StopSign, and is_reconfigured never returns to Some. The reconfiguration content and agreement are unaffected; the defect is that this follower permanently fails to observe the decided reconfiguration after an ordinary lost Prepare plus the documented reconnect call.
counterevidence: The control shows nodes that had not accepted the StopSign sync correctly, so the defect is limited to followers whose accepted prefix already includes the StopSign.
If the follower's Promise participates in the prepare quorum, the leader's decided index may cover the StopSign; whether the accepted over-count would still occur is not measured here.
The StopSign value and the cluster's re-decision are preserved, so this is not loss or divergence of the reconfiguration.
A follower that never accepted the StopSign and never receives the sync would also not report the reconfiguration; that is a different, non-defective case.
limitations: Five nodes, majority quorum, memory storage, unit batch and no snapshots; later resyncs and the new cluster are not exercised.
Leadership is driven by try_become_leader with explicit delivery; BLE timing and real transport are not exercised.
One delayed follower and one control node are sampled; no other ordering of the StopSign sync is explored.
